review.reason:
The artwork maps confidently left-to-right to Holes 1, 2 and 3. One clear greenside bunker-side mismatch needs correction before publication.

Hole 1: The illustration retains the right-bending par 5, substantial left-side lake and relatively narrow fairway. However, its greenside bunkers are clearly on the right, whereas the current geometry has sand on both the right and back-left. Move the greenside bunkering right to match. The shoreline extent and fairway/green proportions are otherwise sufficiently consistent. The lake and inside-corner trees make conservative placement versus an aggressive shortcut meaningful.

Hole 2: Both views show a dry, broad split fairway around a central tree island, a large green and back-left greenside sand. The illustration relocates the fairway bunker toward the left approach, but a general bunker-side adjustment is not a reliable independent correction for that feature. Preserve the playable split routes and currently matching greenside arrangement. The wider right branch offers forgiveness while the left branch provides a different approach angle.

Hole 3: Both views show a substantial lake surrounding the island target, with a separate foreground landing area and left-side bunker. Lake extent and target proportions are close enough to retain. Center-green play provides a sensible alternative to attacking the left-positioned pin, although this remains primarily a carry-control test.

The par-5/4/3 sequence, split routing and contrasting water arrangements provide excellent within-round variety. The island green repeats course 93, but the shorter carry, dry split-fairway hole and dogleg par 5 provide sufficient change. The visible landing spaces and simulated 55/148/26 safe tee options support fair difficulty; the coarse search does not establish it by itself. The requested geometry must be previewed again before approval.

edits.reason: The leftmost illustrated green has clearly right-side sand, unlike the current right and back-left greenside clusters. Concentrate bunkering on the right to match this unambiguous feature while retaining an open left-side approach; leave the substantial left lake unchanged.
